top_choice_rationale: P004 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) credits one identifiable, mature contribution: estimating demand and market power in differentiated-product industries with endogenous prices. The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes approach has about thirty years of re-implementation, criticism and extension, and it is routine in merger review and regulatory counterfactuals. It has also spread into trade, health, environmental and transport economics. That shows it changed what can be measured and decided. The attribution is the most exact of the proposals, with a single origin paper and three authors. The main costs are that Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are not credited, and that the case is methodological, so the citation must stay limited to demand and market-power estimation. I hold this with moderate confidence. I am the only explicit supporter, and that count is not evidence about merit. P003 is second because Melitz and Helpman form a compact, mature pair, though the uncredited priority claims of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum and the welfare-gain critique remain. P001 is third because the China-shock evidence is mature and the Autor, Dorn, Hanson credit is exact, but the shift-share inference and persistence debate and the bundling of the technology and trade strands remain. P002 is fourth because it carries the same bundling and definition problems plus the thematic closeness of Katz's work to the 2023 prize and his appearance in B050. All four award proposals are preferable to no award, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the documented ties are an SSE affiliation shared with committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and co-authors in matching and market design (Svensson, Ehlers, Biró, Teytelboym, Trapp). None of these people is credited in any proposal. KVA and IVA memberships come only from his own CV and homepage and are unverified.
